chapter: Chicago's South Side night life in the early 1920s
title: A black entertainment district and the white audience uptown
summary: Entertainment was concentrated in a mostly black area from 31st to 47th Street, with ballrooms and armories, and white patrons came to the ritzier places as in Harlem.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: All this area, though, was black
then?
MR. CALDWELL: Mostly black. After they came, mostly black, but the white was still living there.
Well, I mean it's extraordinary that the entertainment that was all concentrated -- all this was in a predominantly black setting.

Yes, it was, from 31st and State all the way up to 47th Street. Of course, they had a lot of little theaters, like between -- like the Pickford Theater on -- between Michigan Avenue and Indiana Avenue. See, at that time like Michigan was Michigan Boulevard then when I was a kid because like the J. [Argen] Armour's estate was there. Madame Ernestine Schumann-Heinck, her estate was there. The Rothschilds' estate was there. The Bausch magneto people estate was there.
Well, of course, there were theaters and so forth and houses in the white section probably too.
Oh, yes, definitely.
But I mean this is nevertheless an extraordinary number of -- I mean and there were -- we haven't mentioned ballrooms.
Oh, three ballrooms there.
I mean --
Yeah, now like over at the Armory, we used to play over there, and they had all the big cotillions
and big fraternal organizations, dances at the 370th -- (unintelligible) the eighth Illinois infantry regiment, like the three there under the Sixty-Nine Theater 369th here.
Well, yeah, but the thing that -- of course, a lot of people coming to clubs like Sunset and so forth will be white.
Well, it seemed like the people coming from downtown uptown to Harlem, same way. Yeah, same thing.
Yeah, I mean that would be a fairly important part of it.
Right.
In the ritzier places.
Yeah, that's true.
Yeah, same with the Grand Terrace when they (unintelligible).
Yeah, same with the Grand Terrace.
Yes. Well, that was like Harlem, you know, where the white people would go uptown (unintelligible).
Yeah, that's right. Same thing.
